FDA Fast Track Designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel marks key regulatory milestone in DUBLIN-4 study population of Post-ICI Non-Squamous NSCLC with no actionable genomic alteration (AGA)

Strategic transaction with Biolin provides data from approximately half of DUBLIN-4’s 442 patients and supports the planned interim analysis at 221 PFS events

FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BeyondSpring Inc. (NASDAQ: BYSI) (“BeyondSpring” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage company developing innovative therapies for the treatment of cancer and other diseases, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update highlighting regulatory and strategic progress for Plinabulin and its global Phase 3 DUBLIN-4 trial.

“The third quarter marked an important regulatory and strategic step forward for Plinabulin,” said Min Qiu, Chief Executive Officer of BeyondSpring. “The FDA’s Fast Track designation underscores the significant unmet need for new treatment options for NSCLC patients without AGA and progressing after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, where docetaxel is still the standard of care.  Plinabulin has been shown to improve the tolerability and dose intensity of docetaxel and demonstrated a long-term survival benefit in the previous successful DUBLIN-3 study in second- and third-line EGFR wild-type NSCLC, published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2024.”

Mr. Qiu continued, “With an FDA-aligned Phase 3 design and a strategic transaction with Biolin to support approximately half of DUBLIN-4’s planned 442-patient enrollment, generating quality data from China, we remain focused on advancing the study toward its prespecified interim analysis at 221 progression-free survival events. We believe positive interim results could represent a significant value inflection point for BeyondSpring, as we continue to pursue financing and strategic opportunities to support global execution.”

Recent Regulatory, Clinical and Corporate Highlights

FDA Fast Track designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel in post-ICI non-squamous NSCLC

  • The Company announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Fast Track designation to Plinabulin plus docetaxel for advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable genomic alterations (AGA), following prior anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy.
  • The designated population corresponds to the second- or third-line patient population targeted in the global DUBLIN-4 trial. Fast Track designation may facilitate more frequent FDA interactions and, if applicable criteria are met, rolling review of a future application.

Strategic transaction to fund half of DUBLIN-4’s planned patient enrollment

  • The Company completed the sale of BeyondSpring Ltd., its wholly owned subsidiary that indirectly held the majority equity interest in Dalian Wanchunbulin Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (“Bulin”), to Biolin Investment Limited (“Biolin”) on September 30, 2026, pursuant to a definitive agreement among the parties.
  • As non-cash consideration, Biolin will support the funding of DUBLIN-4 clinical development activities conducted by Bulin at participating sites in China, which are expected to include enrollment of approximately 221 patients, or approximately half of the planned 442-patient global enrollment. BeyondSpring will receive access to clinical data generated from the China portion of the trial.

Third Quarter Financial Results

Continuing operations:

  • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $1.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.1 million was primarily due to a $0.3 million increase in preclinical expenses related to Plinabulin treatment combination research in support of strategic business development and partnership initiatives, partially offset by lower patent-related legal services and drug manufacturing costs.
  • General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $1.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.3 million was primarily due to an increase in legal fees related to financing activities and higher consulting expenses related to accounting advisory and audit services, partially offset by lower personnel-related and travel expenses.
  • Net loss was $2.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
  • Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were $0.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $4.0 million as of December 31, 2025.

Year-to-Date Financial Results

Continuing operations:

  • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $3.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.4 million was primarily due to expanded drug manufacturing activities and increased preclinical Plinabulin treatment combination research, partially offset by lower patent-related legal services and personnel-related expenses.
  • General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $2.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease of $0.5 million was primarily due to lower personnel-related expenses, mainly from lower incentive compensation and share-based compensation, as well as lower professional service expenses in legal advisory and lower travel and entertainment expenses.
  • Net loss was $5.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

About BeyondSpring
BeyondSpring (NASDAQ: BYSI) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class therapies for cancers with high unmet needs. Its lead asset, Plinabulin, has been studied in more than 700 cancer patients and is in late-stage development across multiple cancer indications. Plinabulin’s novel mechanism as a GEF-H1 agonist with dendritic cell maturation benefit supports both anticancer activity and immune modulation, offering a unique approach to resensitizing tumors that have progressed on checkpoint inhibitors. In addition, it has the potential to synergize with chemotherapy, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), radiation, and checkpoint inhibitors. BeyondSpring is also an early incubator of and maintains an equity interest in SEED Therapeutics, a clinical-stage targeted protein degradation molecular glue company with investments from Eli Lilly and Eisai. Learn more at beyondspringpharma.com.

About Plinabulin and the Clinical Rationale for the DUBLIN-4 Trial
Plinabulin is a late-stage, first-in-class investigational GEF-H1 agonist with a differentiated mechanism of action that includes dendritic cell maturation, anti-angiogenic activity and mitigation of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. To date, more than 700 cancer patients have been treated with Plinabulin across multiple clinical programs in various cancer types, demonstrating an extensive clinical safety database.

The post-ICI setting remains difficult to treat: 12 Phase 3 trials evaluating different treatment approaches against docetaxel, including four involving ADCs, have failed to demonstrate an overall survival benefit over docetaxel.

In the Phase 3 DUBLIN-3 trial, published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2024, Plinabulin combined with docetaxel demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in OS in second- and third-line EGFR wild-type NSCLC vs. docetaxel alone (n=559), showing superior OS benefit in non-squamous patients (n=332, OS HR 0.72, p=0.0078). The combination also demonstrated statistically significant improvements compared to docetaxel alone, including doubling the 2-year and 3-year survival rates and improvements in PFS and ORR, while also significantly reducing grade 4 neutropenia (p<0.0001).

Importantly, a post hoc analysis of the DUBLIN-3 post-ICI subgroup showed a median OS of 15.8 months with Plinabulin plus docetaxel versus 11.7 months with docetaxel alone (HR 0.55), with ORR of 18.2% versus 8.0%, respectively. These findings support the clinical rationale for Plinabulin’s differentiated dendritic cell maturation mechanism and its further evaluation in DUBLIN-4.

This rationale was further supported by prospective data from the Phase 2 Study 303 (n=47), presented at ASCO 2026. In patients with NSCLC whose disease had progressed following PD-1 inhibitor treatment, the combination of Plinabulin, docetaxel and a PD-1 inhibitor demonstrated encouraging anticancer activity. With a median follow-up of 28.8 months, the Plinabulin combination showed a median PFS of 7.0 months, a disease control rate of 79.5%, and a confirmed ORR of 18.2%, with a 2-year OS rate of 58%, nearly double the historical rate reported with docetaxel in a similar patient population.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 13, 2026) - NuGen Medical Devices Inc. (TSXV: NGMD) ("NuGen" or the "Company"), a developer of needle-free drug delivery technology, provides an update regarding its Canadian medical device licence for the InsuJet™ needle-free insulin injection system.

Further to the Company's news release dated February 5, 2026, Health Canada has issued a Notice of Refusal in respect of the Company's Class II medical device licence application no. 407982. As previously disclosed, the Company's prior Canadian medical device licence had lapsed and sales in Canada were halted while the new application was under review. Sales and further supply of InsuJet in Canada remain halted.

Health Canada determined that the clinical evidence submitted with the application was insufficient to demonstrate compliance with certain safety and effectiveness requirements under sections 11, 12 and 13 of the Canadian Medical Devices Regulations. The matters identified by Health Canada include the need for additional evidence concerning insulin-specific clinical performance, bioequivalence or alternatively evidence supporting the safety and effectiveness of insulin therapy using the device, longer-term glycemic control and safety endpoints, reliable patient self-administration, and injection performance.

The Notice of Refusal applies to the Canadian application and does not, by itself, amend the regulatory status of InsuJet in jurisdictions outside Canada. NuGen continues to maintain registrations and commercial activities in a number of markets outside Canada, subject in each case to applicable local regulatory requirements.

The Notice of Refusal does not state that InsuJet is unsafe or ineffective. It states that the evidence submitted was insufficient to demonstrate that the requirements applicable to the Canadian application and its proposed use with NovoRapid insulin had been met. Investors should not interpret this distinction as an assurance that a future Canadian application will be approved.

Canadian Market and Existing Users

Based on discussions with the Company's Canadian regulatory representative, the Notice of Refusal does not require a recall of InsuJet devices previously lawfully imported and sold in Canada while the applicable licence was active. The Company has also been advised that existing Canadian users are not required to discontinue use of devices already supplied.

Clinical Evidence and Regulatory Path Forward

NuGen intends to review the Notice of Refusal with its regulatory and clinical advisers and to continue discussions with Health Canada concerning the evidence that may be required for a future submission. Subject to available funding, final protocol design, regulatory feedback and other factors, the Company currently intends to incorporate relevant elements of Health Canada's feedback into clinical evidence-generation activities in connection with its next-generation needle-free injector platform.

Management Comment

"We are disappointed with Health Canada's decision, but the Notice of Refusal provides greater clarity regarding the additional clinical evidence required for a future Canadian application," said Liang Lin, Chief Executive Officer of NuGen. "We intend to consider these requirements as part of our planned clinical program for our next-generation needle-free technology. While sales and further supply in Canada remain halted, we remain committed to working with our regulatory and clinical partners to address Health Canada's requirements and pursue a path back to the Canadian market."

About NuGen Medical Devices

NuGen develops next-generation needle-free devices for subcutaneous drug delivery. Its flagship InsuJet™ system has been registered in numerous international markets and is designed to provide an alternative to conventional needle-based injections.
